ratings.reason: The forward break is now a usable close counter: a visible-charge normal-input response kept the guard directly ahead for ADS and a subsequent hit. The marker no longer covers the optic. A new reserved-row collision and the enormous induction tutorial sign keep central presentation crowded, while the emissive optic/ring, basic model forms and shared courtyard still limit fidelity and content. A short opening check does not establish whole-mission enjoyment or perfection.

findings.recommendation: Prefer fading a central distant objective during ADS at an active visible threat while retaining radar and other goal markers, or implement collision-aware HUD placement. Avoid forcing every central marker into another fixed crowded row.

findings.finding: After a successful close break and ADS, the world INDUCTION GUARD sign spans most of the upper central view and the very bright upper optic/ring dominate the enemy silhouette. The phase confirmation overlays the sign's instruction text.
findings.recommendation: Consider reducing/dismissing the teaching signage after the first resolved guard encounter and refine emissive values/optic anatomy. Preserve the clear charge/armor state distinction. This is presentation feedback, not proof of a mechanical failure.

limitations: Short opening/targeting review, not a complete mission or broad balance study.
Prior knowledge and automated visible-label timing advantage the controller.
No human enjoyment/audio validation, production animation/content work, hardware performance certification or broad accessibility audit.
